solutionSql:
SELECT d.shipment_id, COUNT(*) AS distinct_scans
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT sc.shipment_id, sc.status, sc.occurred_at
  FROM staging_scans AS sc
  JOIN shipments AS s ON s.id = sc.shipment_id
  WHERE sc.status IS NOT NULL
) AS d
GROUP BY d.shipment_id
ORDER BY d.shipment_id;

ambiguities.phrase: two scans are the same when they have the same status and occurred_at
ambiguities.readingChosen: Deduplicate on (shipment_id, status, occurred_at) with SELECT DISTINCT, ignoring the scan id; a NULL occurred_at is kept and two scans with the same status and both NULL occurred_at count as one.
ambiguities.alternativeReading: Treat a NULL occurred_at as not comparable (each such scan counted separately) or drop it, e.g. COUNT(DISTINCT status || occurred_at) would skip it.

ambiguities.phrase: A scan for a shipment that does not exist is not counted
ambiguities.readingChosen: Inner join to shipments, which also drops scans with a NULL shipment_id.
ambiguities.alternativeReading: Only drop non-NULL ids missing from shipments; a NULL shipment_id would then form its own group.

notes: Sample: 41 scans, 5 orphan ids, 3 NULL-status scans on existing shipments, one exact duplicate (shipment 120) leave 32 shipments with 1 distinct scan each. Dedup ignores scan id. Shipments with only NULL-status scans (33, 86, 167) are absent.
